baseline_scope: The integrated upstream authentication/main changes are baseline inputs, not implementation authored or reviewed as part of this design-entry repair.
scope: Native design-stage progress and explicit next actions; visible service execution prerequisites; confirmed local specification handoff through native host callables into Maliang; immutable project/account/conversation/revision binding, private persistence and append idempotency; truthful reserved/created states; isolated regressions and default CI invocation.

findings.problem: The first implementation checked drafts only in the selected source stage, so an earlier unsaved stage could be ignored when preparing an older confirmed specification.
findings.resolution: All design stages are checked before choosing a confirmed direction or detailed design. The native regression covers an earlier unsaved direction after all saved stages were confirmed.

findings.problem: The new top action targeted a hidden launch button when an execution already existed.
findings.resolution: Existing execution uses the progress caption and scrolls to the visible execution status; an unlaunched requirement still targets launch prerequisites.

findings.problem: Nullable title/acceptance became null marker strings; final native verification additionally found that an empty direction title did not fall back to the conversation title.
findings.resolution: Null or blank titles fall back to the conversation title; absent acceptance becomes an empty string. Nonblank authored titles retain their original text. Final integrated native verification passes the real service response case.

findings.problem: A returned revision was offered for confirmation even though the service requires a new revision.
findings.resolution: Confirmation is disabled for returned revisions and Next explains revision/save requirements. The native HTTP regression returns a plan, edits it, saves a new revision and only then confirms.

findings.problem: The reservation was originally persisted as node_created before graph append, causing a crash window to falsely report successful creation.
findings.resolution: Durable node_reserved precedes append; node_created is persisted only after actual append. Unknown reservations never replay. Terminal write failure reports the actual in-memory append and retained unknown durable state. Final compiled regression covers both fault windows.

findings.problem: The new compiled handoff regression initially existed only as a standalone runner.
findings.resolution: The standard native-shell local-contract branch now invokes it, checks exit/result and exact binary digest, and includes its product/test inputs in source-drift verification.

findings.problem: Using a null get_meta default for optional host callbacks produced three new missing-metadata errors in the standalone controller fixture.
findings.resolution: Both optional callbacks use an empty Callable default. Final source contract passes 43 checks without either missing-metadata error, and the final compiled handoff passes 27 checks.

review_checks: Stage switching and Next re-read current controller state. Generation, saving, confirmation and publication remain separate explicit actions; server stage/version/approval gates remain intact.
Viewer, busy, unsaved-draft and missing-service states are explained. Existing execution navigates to visible status; historical revisions are folded without deleting content.

Native and Maliang preparation validate the entire frozen snapshot, including current project, identity scope, conversation, stage, revision, title, body and acceptance. Append revalidates the source; identity reset clears the temporary card including its title.

Persisted IDs bind project, scope, conversation, stage and revision. The digest binds the complete snapshot. Bounded schema validation, atomic replacement and an exclusive directory lock reject corrupt or conflicting records and cooperating concurrent writers.

The workbench preserves existing graph content and applies valid pending inspector edits before appending one normal text-to-mesh node. Busy execution, template editing and duplicate node IDs are rejected. Preparation and append do not start a job, overwrite model settings or grant consultation tools.

Preparation is distinct from production. Existing workspace-service execution remains a separate path and is labeled with its location; local chat availability is not treated as proof that the service or mesh backend is ready.
The optional real CLI probe remains isolated/read-only. This reviewer read its receipt and did not invoke a real provider or operate the user application.

baseline_updates.impact_review: The upstream session controller changes device-session enrollment, legacy credential migration and same-account reauthentication retention. The native entry consumes its identity, scope and reset signals, so this is a read dependency overlap. The scope-key calculation and identity-reset/activation signal contract remain unchanged. The new handoff still compares the current full snapshot and clears on identity reset. Upstream server/auth/repository behavior retains its own review responsibility; this amendment does not independently reapprove that separate feature.
